arrived in Shanghai on the s.s. "Tegelberg" on

Arrived Hong Kong from New York on Clipper via San Francisco on

January 26th 1939 - took plane in Hanoi (French Indo-China) for

February 4th 1939 - took plane in Kunming for Hanoi (His passport

February 14 1939 left Dong Dang (frontier of Tonkin and Kwangsi) in

fired at his tyres whereupon he stopped. Was immediately arrested
tried in French Court at Lang-Son (Tonkin, Indochina), March 21, 1939.
convicted on charge "Menace with arm to Agents of the Law" fined 500
gold francs and given a suspended jail sentence of six months.
April 6th 1939 he left Hanoi by plane "Dorado" for Hong Kong.
April 14th 1939 he returned from Hongkong to Hanoi on plane "Delphines".
April 23, 1939 he returned Hongkong from Hanoi by plane. While in
Hongkong he went to Macao where he tried to purchase a Portuguese
passport for which he offered M$4000. He failed to obtain one.
April 26th 1939 (about) he left Hongkong for Shanghai.
May 19th 1939 he arrived Hongkong from Shanghai on the S.S. "Canto
Rosso" - went to Gloucester Hotel where he occupied Room 402 under
name E. Hockelmann. (While in Shanghai he evidently obtained possession
of a false passport.)
May 19th 1939 he entered the Far Memorial Hospital, Hongkong
ostensibly for a rest.
May 28, 1939 left hospital suddenly stating he was going to Nanning
via Macao. No evidence he went to Nanning and believe he went
Shanghai where he is now (Nov. 16, 1939) living at 183 Route Puginy,
apt 22, French Concession.

1939年4月23日，他乘飞机从河内返回香港。在香港期间，他去了澳门，试图购买一本葡萄牙护照，出价4000澳门元。但他未能买到。
1939年4月26日（左右），他离开香港前往上海。

1939年5月19日，他进入香港远东纪念医院（Far Memorial Hospital），名义上是去休养。
1939年5月28日，他突然离开医院，声称将经澳门前往南宁。没有证据表明他去了南宁，相信他去了上海，他目前（1939年11月16日）住在法租界蒲石路183号22室。

Lieutenant-Commander of a German U-Boat.
The outbreak of the World War found Eckelmann rooming with a
family in Hoboken, New Jersey. He endeavored to return to his
fatherland on a Swedish boat but was picked up by the Russians
and sent to a concentration camp somewhere in Siberia from where
he escaped by clinging to the bottom of a railway carriage and
with the aid of a Swedish nurse, who disguised him as a wounded
Russian, managed to gain a Baltic seaport, where he boarded a
Swedish vessel as a stowaway, eventually landing safely in Germany.
He enlisted in the German Navy where he studied wireless telegraphy
and later became an operator. While transmitting coded messages
he became interested in codes and found he could readily decode
the messages he was transmitting. He reported the fact to his
commanding officer and tried to point out the apparent weakness
in the code. As a result he was summoned to headquarters in Berlin
and assigned the task of creating an unbreakable code. After
three months he accomplished this remarkable feat evolving a
code with 16 million possibilities, possible of being changed at
a minute's notice and he maintains this code has never been solved.
Later made codes for Krupps and other large steel mills, etc.
When the war ended and conditions in Germany became unsettled,
subject, due to lack of commercial training, etc., found it
difficult to adjust himself and accepted an offer of the Japanese
Government to go to Japan to give military instructions, where he
remained until 1937. Some time in 1937 he came to China where
he came under CHIANG KAI SHEK served as instructor at the

period of his troubles with the Communists; served as adviser to

世界大战爆发时，埃克尔曼（Eckelmann）寄宿在新泽西州霍博肯的一户家庭中。他试图乘坐一艘瑞典船只返回祖国，但被俄国人抓获，并被送往西伯利亚某处的集中营，他从那里逃脱，方法是紧抓在一节铁路车厢底部，并在一位瑞典护士的帮助下——该护士将他伪装成受伤的俄国人——设法到达波罗的海的一个海港，在那里他作为偷渡者登上一艘瑞典船只，最终安全抵达德国。
他加入德国海军，学习无线电报务，后来成为报务员。在发送编码信息时，他对密码产生了兴趣，并发现自己可以轻易解码他正在发送的信息。他将这一事实报告给指挥官，并试图指出该密码明显的弱点。结果，他被召至柏林总部，并受命创造一种不可破译的密码。三个月后，他完成了这一非凡壮举，设计出一种拥有1600万种可能性的密码，可以在一分钟内更改，他坚称这种密码从未被破解。
后来，他为克虏伯（Krupps）和其他大型钢铁厂等编制密码。
当战争结束且德国局势动荡时，由于缺乏商业训练等原因，当事人发现难以适应，于是接受了日本政府的邀请前往日本提供军事指导，他在那里一直待到1937年。1937年的某个时候，他来到中国，投奔蒋介石，在广州黄埔军校担任教官；在蒋介石与共产党发生冲突期间，他随侍在侧；担任蒋介石和张作霖元帅的顾问；为中国政府编制专用密码，并为蒋介石执行特殊任务；例如：经过数月准备和学习藏语后，他伪装成聋哑理发师访问拉萨，以探听民众对蒋介石的态度；他在禁毒运动中从事专门的调查工作，以阻止鸦片的进口和使用；他陪同中国代表团参加日内瓦国际联盟会议。

The importance of absolute secrecy was stressed,
due to the value of the shipments and the possible
dangers involved. Lokelmann stated, further, that
certain expenses, particularly the insurance
premium, would have to be advanced by himself, so
as to hide the identity of his principals and that
he had no confidence in the individuals in New York
who were willing to back him. On the otherhand, if
he were to have dependable coworkers, he was confident
that he could handle the entire financing himself.
provided he could get advances not exceeding
25,000 U. S. This was to be accomplished by having
his coworker follow him to Hongkong in order to bring
the 16 cases back to New York. An amount sufficient
to defray any additional expenses could then readily
be raised against this first shipment (the 16 cases)
as security.

We consulted the GALLERIES and were assured that there was no doubt
as to the existence of these treasures and that the entire matter
appeared to be bona-fide. We asked Lokelmann for proof of his
authority. He accordingly produced a batch of cables dating back
to the original negotiations in 1937 - obviously genuine cables,
but all in code. He translated the cables covering the points
we wish to have verified and finally exposed the code key enabling
us to check his translations at random. They tallied exactly. We
realized they might have been sent by a confederate but had no
reason to be suspicious. Our attempts to locate these cables
since Lokelmann's disappearance have proven unsuccessful.

When attempts to cover marine insurance in New York came to naught,
due to the amount involved and his inability to disclose details,
he cabled to China and advised us that the CHINESE GOVERNMENT itself
had arranged to cover up to 30,000,000 U.S.$, the insurance companies
not to be notified as to details until the carrying steamer was
under way 60 hours.
Time seemed to be important. We accordingly made an agreement with
Lokelmann to act for him in New York in his dealings with the
American Art Galleries, and gave him the required cash advance of
29,000 U.S.$ in all.

我们咨询了美国艺术画廊（American Art Galleries），并得到保证，这些珍宝的存在毫无疑问，且整个事件似乎是真实可信的。我们要求洛克尔曼提供其授权证明。因此，他出示了一批可追溯至1937年最初谈判时期的电报——显然是真实的电报，但全部采用密码编写。他翻译了我们希望核实要点的电报，并最终公开了密码本，使我们能够随机核对他的译文。译文完全吻合。我们意识到这些电报可能是由同伙发送的，但没有理由产生怀疑。自洛克尔曼失踪以来，我们试图查找这些电报的努力均未成功。

当在纽约投保海运保险的努力因涉及金额巨大且他无法披露细节而告吹时，他向中国发电报，并告知我们中国政府本身已安排承保高达3,000万美元的保险，且在承运轮船启航60小时内，保险公司不会获知细节。
时间似乎至关重要。因此，我们与洛克尔曼达成协议，代表他在纽约与美国艺术画廊进行交易，并向他提供了总计29,000美元的所需预付款。
以下是斯特恩兄弟公司（Stern Bros）收到的来自洛克尔曼的电报摘录。

1月5日 - 发自香港：指示笔者改乘下一班“飞剪”号（Clipper）飞机，并告知他将于下周一与委座（Generalissimo）会晤。同日，他寄出一封航空信确认上述事项，并告知笔者需携带何种衣物，同时提醒笔者核对“飞剪”号飞机的时刻表，因为这些时刻表可能会受到新型波音飞机的影响。他补充说，笔者在将香港的箱子运抵美国后，随后应返回远东，并陪同洛克尔曼经新加坡和苏伊士运河运送主要货物。他建议我们不要期待收到太多电报，因为费用几乎高得令人望而却步——每字5.40美元（无疑是港币）。

1月6日 -

pages.en:
Jan. 6th - From Hongkong: A answer to our cable of Jany. 5th
advising him that the Galleries requested two weeks'
notice in case of any cash demands. He replied that
he needed no money, that his funds were ample. ( As a
matter of fact, he never asked the Galleries for money
although he could have obtained it, and had arranged
for such a contingency.) He again stressed the
necessity of immediate action in connection with his
personal insurance, because of the danger attending his
mission.

Jan. 8th- From Hongkong: reply to our cable and confirming that
shipments were insured right up to warehouse in New York.
He added "hurry hurry my insurance going soon dangerous
trip". On the same day, however, we cabled him that the
insurance had been refused, presumably because the companies
had checked through their Shanghai office and had doubted
the alleged personal nature of his trip, due to his past
activities.

Jan. 9th - From Hongkong: stated he could cover $60,000 insurance with
Manufacturers' Life. He asked our O.K., which we gave him.

Jan. 11th - From Hongkong: asked us to send premium direct to the
insurance company in Hongkong, which would issue interim
policies, valid until the actual policies were issued by
the headoffices. We cabled the remittance.

Jan. 14th - From Hongkong: advised that the headoffice had refused to
accept and that the policy was accordingly cancelled; but
that he had covered the same amount definitely with Lloyds,
including aviation and war risks. We have the policy.
He asked to be advised of the exact date when the Clipper,
bringing the writer, would depart from San Francisco; for
he was leaving for Haiphong the next day.

Jan. 24th - From Hanoi: Cabled that the bombing of Chungking had
necessitated a change in plans and that he had been ordered
to return to Chungking at once. He instructed the writer
to cancel his Clipper reservation for Feby. 1st and to
make a new one for Feby. 2nd. He added that he would
report further as soon as possible after his return to the
"Tonkin border".

Feb. 1st - From Chungking: advised he was going to Hanoi on Friday to
buy gasoline, that he would return to Chungking end of the
following week, and that he would leave Chungking with the
caravan twelve days later. He added that he would bring the
entire shipment himself via Singapore and Suez by regular
scheduled steamer. (He had made an investigation into the
cost of specially chartered steamers prior to his departure
from New York and had discussed this possibility with us).
He asked us to request the Galleries to be prepared to
remit $7000 to Singapore for freight, but not to remit until
so instructed. He said a reply would reach him in Hanoi.
We accordingly cabled him at the Galleries' suggestion to
inquire whether the freight could be paid here on arrival,
since the Hongkong cases were not available as security.

Feb. 7th - From Hanoi: He said that he was returning that night to
Chungking, whence he would depart in three weeks, and that
instructions for us would follow on his return to Hanoi.
He told the writer not to come to Hongkong, but to be
prepared to render him assistance at French ports (presumably
Marseilles). He added that the freight could be paid to
the agent in New York, but begged us to see that there be
no hitch arising from a possible delay in payment.

Feb. 8th -
pages.zh:
1月6日 - 发自香港：回复我们1月5日的电报，告知他画廊要求如有现金需求需提前两周通知。他回复说不需要钱，他的资金充足。（事实上，他从未向画廊要钱，尽管他本可以拿到，并已为此类意外情况做好了安排。）他再次强调，由于他的任务伴随危险，必须立即就其个人保险采取行动。

1月8日 - 发自香港：回复我们的电报，并确认货物已投保至纽约仓库。他补充道：“ hurry hurry my insurance going soon dangerous trip”（快点快点我的保险快到期了旅途危险）。然而，就在同一天，我们给他发去电报，称保险已被拒绝，大概是因为各保险公司通过其上海办事处进行了核查，并因其过去的活动而怀疑他所声称的此次行程的个人性质。

1月9日 - 发自香港：称他可以通过宏利人寿保险公司（Manufacturers' Life）投保60,000美元。他征求我们的同意，我们予以批准。

1月11日 - 发自香港：要求我们将保费直接汇给香港的保险公司，该公司将签发临时保单，在总公司签发正式保单之前有效。我们电汇了汇款。

1月14日 - 发自香港：告知总公司拒绝接受，因此保单已取消；但他已明确通过劳合社（Lloyds）投保了相同金额，包括航空险和战争险。我们要持有该保单。他要求告知搭载笔者的“飞剪”号飞机从旧金山起飞的确切日期；因为他第二天就要动身前往海防。

1月24日 - 发自河内：发电报称，对重庆的轰炸导致计划变更，他已奉命立即返回重庆。他指示笔者取消2月1日的“飞剪”号预订，并重新预订2月2日的航班。他补充说，一旦回到“东京湾边境”，他将尽快进一步报告。

2月1日 - 发自重庆：告知他将于周五前往河内购买汽油，将于下周周末返回重庆，并于十二天后随商队离开重庆。他补充说，他将亲自经由新加坡和苏伊士运河，通过定期班轮运送整批货物。（他在离开纽约前曾调查过特别包租轮船的费用，并与我们要讨论过这种可能性。）他要求我们请画廊准备向新加坡汇付7,000美元运费，但在接到指示前不要汇款。他说回复将在河内收到。因此，根据画廊的建议，我们给他发去电报，询问是否可以在货物抵达时在此地支付运费，因为香港的箱子不能作为抵押品。

2月7日 - 发自河内：他说他当晚将返回重庆，三周后将从那里出发，待他返回河内后会向我们发出指示。他告诉笔者不要来香港，而要准备好在法国港口（大概是马赛）为他提供协助。他补充说，运费可以支付给纽约的代理人，但恳请我们确保不会因付款可能延迟而出现任何差错。

2月8日 -

pages.en:
- 5 -

Feb. 8th - From Hanoi: Cabled "require Indochine duty bond seven
hundred U. S. dollars. Remit immediately Bank of China,
Hanoi. Lost already two days". Our bank being closed,
we resitted the following day.
Feb.11th - From Hanoi: Advised that remittance had not arrived and
requested name of the bank through whom the remittance had
been sent. We replied that the delay was occasioned by the
fact that the remittance had been relayed via Paris.
March 11 - From Hanoi: Cabled 'Delayed about two weeks unforeseen pass
formalities Yunnanfu customs Indochina'.
Several days later we cabled him that we were interested in
obtaining a share of the contracts that would be placed in
the future in connection with Chinese reconstruction require-
ments and asked his co-operation.
Mar.16th - From Hanoi: Cabled he was very much interested and would do
his utmost.
Mar.16th - From Hanoi: Advised that French and German competition was
strong and that long terms were being offered. He named some
of the German firms that were competing. He suggested his
flying at once to Sian and Chungking, stating that the
Generalissimo would listen to him at any time provided he
could offer the same credit terms as others. He pointed out
that the best opportunities lay in the Yunnan province. He
requested a remittance of one thousand dollars and advised us
that he was leaving via Singapore and Rangoon on April 6th.
We sent the remittance, but advised against the Sian trip,
since we felt that the long terms were then impossible.
Mar.19th - From Hanoi: Inquired how much our friends could finance,
stating that he thought the U.S. loan to the Chinese had been
absorbed.
Mar.10th - From Hanoi: Advised the writer to meet him in Genoa or
Marseilles, and added that cable instructions would follow in
three weeks.
Apr. 4th - From Hanoi: Wired that it was impossible for him to leave as
planned in his cable of March 16th, as the S/S "Canton", which
had booked the cargo, had had a collision. (We checked this
and found it correct). Besides, he said, the "French transit
trouble" was still unsettled. He added that he would try to
get another boat end of April and that if he could not make a
satisfactory booking in Hanoi, he would fly to Hongkong in
order to make arrangements there. He said that several
German firms (whom he named) were working hard to get the
Yunnan business and were offering twelve months' terms after
delivery. He said that contracts amounting to over two million
English pounds were at stake and that we should let him know
whether we were interested, as he was going to see the
Generalissimo soon.
Apr. 5th - He cabled in answer to our inquiry that both vessels had been
slightly damaged, and that he was sending us a confidential
airmail letter giving details we had requested. (This cable
was from Hanoi).
Apr.11th - From Hongkong: Airmail letter advised that shipment would
consist of 345 cases, 193.7 tons, 24,319 items, and that the
insured value was U.S. $37,750,000. He added that he had
travelled more than 16,000 km. over the worst roads ever built
and 18,000 km. by air; that his party had been bombed four
times in the Kwangsi, Kweichow and Szechuan provinces; that
he had been shot at by the French on arriving at the Indo-
chinese border; and that in general the French were causing
him unthinkable difficulties. He said that "in order to bluff
the French and the Japs, I have been arrested pro forma by
the Chinese, and the most wonderful result happened; they
believed it!" He said he had lost 16 men and that he had
accidentally killed one himself, when he ran into his car during
the excitement attending an air raid by the Japs between
Lichow

- 5 -

2月8日 - 发自河内：发电报称“需要印度支那关税保证金七百美元。立即汇至中国银行河内分行。已经损失两天”。由于我们的银行关门，我们于次日重新汇款。
2月11日 - 发自河内：告知汇款尚未到达，并要求提供汇款所经银行的名称。我们回复说，延误是因为汇款是通过巴黎转送的。
3月11日 - 发自河内：发电报称“因云南府海关印度支那边境不可预见的通关手续，延误约两周”。
几天后，我们给他发去电报，表示我们有兴趣获得未来与中国重建需求相关的合同份额，并请求他的合作。
3月16日 - 发自河内：发电报称他非常感兴趣，并将竭尽全力。
3月16日 - 发自河内：告知法国和德国的竞争很激烈，且对方提供长期付款条件。他列举了一些参与竞争的德国公司。他建议立即飞往西安和重庆，称只要他能提供与其他人相同的信用条件，委座随时都会听取他的意见。他指出，最好的机会在于云南省。他要求汇款一千美元，并告知我们将于4月6日经新加坡和仰光离开。我们汇出了款项，但建议不要进行西安之行，因为我们认为当时长期付款条件是不可能的。
3月19日 - 发自河内：询问我们的朋友能提供多少融资，称他认为美国对华贷款已被吸收殆尽。
3月10日 - 发自河内：建议笔者在热那亚或马赛与他见面，并补充说电报指示将在三周内随后发出。
4月4日 - 发自河内：发电报称，正如他3月16日电报中计划的那样，他无法离开，因为已预订货物的“广东”号轮船（S/S "Canton"）发生了碰撞。（我们对此进行了核实，发现属实）。此外，他说，“法国过境问题”仍未解决。他补充说，他将尝试在4月底搭乘另一艘船，如果他在河内无法做出令人满意的预订，他将飞往香港在那里做出安排。他说几家德国公司（他列出了名字）正在努力争取云南的业务，并提供交货后十二个月的付款期限。他说涉及的合同金额超过两百万英镑，我们应该让他知道是否感兴趣，因为他很快就要去见委座。
4月5日 - 他回复我们的询问发电报称，两艘船均受到轻微损坏，并且他正寄给我们一封机密航空信，提供我们要求的细节。（这封电报发自河内）。
4月11日 - 发自香港：航空信告知，货物将由345箱组成，重193.7吨，共24,319件物品，投保价值为37,750,000美元。他补充说，他行驶了超过16,000公里的最糟糕的道路，并飞行了18,000公里；他的团队在广西、贵州和四川省被轰炸了四次；他在抵达印度支那边境时遭到法国人的射击；总的来说，法国人给他造成了难以想象的困难。他说，“为了欺骗法国人和日本人，我被中国人形式上逮捕了，结果妙极了；他们相信了！”他说他失去了16名手下，并且他自己意外杀死了一人，当时在日军空袭引起的混乱中，他撞上了自己的汽车，地点在李州（Lichow）

...tion and ...ing. He stated that Mrs. Tailing Sai-she was
then in Hongkong, and that he would leave with her in one or
two days to fly to the Generalissimo to get his permission
to change the route; for if the latter consented, he would go
via the Burma road to Rangoon, and would arrange to ship
everything by the President Line, so as to avoid the necessity
of any transshipment in Genoa or Marseille; and that he would
then arrive in New York three weeks later (presumably by plane.
He mentioned that he had seen the S/S "Canton" and S/S
"Marechal Joffre", which had been in collision, and that, while
the damage was not great, it would result in a delay of 3-4
weeks. He expressed keen disappointment that the collision
had prevented his being already under way. He again complained
of the high cable costs and asked us not to demand unnecessary
replies. As to his personal insurance, he had asked Bilman &
Co. to extend it another six weeks. (He received official notice
direct from Lloyds in London in due course of time).
pr.21th-from Hongkong: Cabled: "Remit HK$1 250 extension Lloyds policy".
He did this.
pr.24th-from Hanoi: Cabled reply to Galleries' request for copy of
marine policy. Stated he could not decide this himself, but
would have to refer it to headquarters. In any event, this
could not be done until after the arrival of the shipment at
port.
pr.25th-from Hanoi: Cabled for definite instructions regarding credit
terms. He said he was anxious to help, but his time was short,
as he was going to see the Generalissimo for the last time on
April 3rd. He spent much time - even in Washington - trying
to solve the credit problem. He eventually hit upon a possible
solution, but were never able to pass the information to
Eckelmann, as we did not contact him again.
pr.19th-from Hanoi: This cable was apparently sent by a coworker in
Hanoi in reply to an inquiry of ours regarding the disposition
of some code books in Canada belonging to Eckelmann. The party
answered after referring it to Eckelmann in Yunnan. He also
stated that other answers to our cables would be forthcoming
"after three weeks arrival southport". Then the party added:
"Stop cabling everybody leaving tomorrow communicate first
opportunity".
any kind-from Hongkong: Cabled "Arriving July 18 President Hayes
Instructions Follow". This is the last direct word we have
had from Eckelmann.

Wire cross
continue:
We shall omit details as to our efforts to contact him. Needless
to say, they were unsuccessful, and he did not return to New
York. A cable sent c/o Area office - Hongkong on May 23, 1939,
remained undelivered and we received notice "Addressee gone
Chungking for few days. Will retender upon return." A later
inquiry brought the answer "Addressee left not returned" (Note -
Cable address "Areaoffice Hongkong" is registered under name
"Hongkong Hotels Company".) Our cabled enquiry to M/s. A. Kaller
& Co. Ltd., Hongkong, resulted in following reply: "According
Police Records, Eckelmann left Hongkong May 23. Supposed gone
Nanning, but police under impression he went elsewhere. Actual
whereabouts unknown."
Bilman & Co., Ltd., Hongkong, who placed his personal insurance
replied: "The last we heard was that Eckelmann left Hongkong
on or about the 22nd May for Haiphong."

……tion 和 ……ing。他称，Tailing Sai-she 夫人当时在香港，他将于一两天内与她一同乘飞机去见委员长，以获准改变路线；因为如果后者同意，他将经缅甸公路前往仰光，并安排通过“总统轮船公司”（President Line）装运所有货物，从而避免在热那亚或马赛进行任何转运的必要；随后他将在三周后抵达纽约（推测是乘飞机）。他提到他曾见过发生碰撞的“广东”号轮船（S/S "Canton"）和“马雷夏尔·约夫尔”号轮船（S/S "Marechal Joffre"），虽然损坏不大，但会导致3至4周的延误。他对因碰撞而未能早日启程表示极度失望。他再次抱怨电报费用高昂，并要求我们不要索取不必要的回复。关于其个人保险，他已要求 Bilman & Co. 公司将保险期再延长六周。（他随后按时收到了来自伦敦劳合社的直接正式通知）。
pr.21th-自香港：发电：“汇港币1,250元以续延劳合社保单”。
他照办了。
pr.24th-自河内：复电回应 Galleries 公司索取海运保单副本的请求。称他本人无法决定此事，必须上报总部。无论如何，此事只能在货物抵港后才能办理。
pr.25th-自河内：发电索取关于信用条款的确切指示。他说他很乐意帮忙，但时间紧迫，因为他将于4月3日最后一次去见委员长。他花费了大量时间——甚至在华盛顿期间——试图解决信用问题。他最终想出了一个可能的解决方案，但由于我们未再与他联系，始终未能将该信息传递给 Eckelmann。
pr.19th-自河内：此电报显然由河内的一位同事发出，以回复我们就处置属于 Eckelmann 存于加拿大的一些密码本一事提出的查询。该当事人在咨询了位于云南的 Eckelmann 后予以答复。他还表示，对我们其他电报的答复将在“抵达南部港口三周后”发出。随后该当事人补充道：“停止向所有人发电报 明日离开 有机会即联系”。
any kind-自香港：发电：“7月18日抵 总统海斯号 听候指示”。这是我们从 Eckelmann 那里收到的最后直接消息。

电报交叉
继续：
我们将省略关于我们试图联系他的细节。不用说，这些努力均未成功，他也未返回纽约。1939年5月23日发往香港地区办事处转交的一封电报未被送达，我们收到通知：“收件人已去重庆数日。返回后将重新投递。”随后的查询得到的答复是：“收件人已离开，未返回”（注——电报地址“Areaoffice Hongkong”注册在“Hongkong Hotels Company”名下。）我们向香港 A. Kaller & Co. Ltd. 公司发出的电报查询，得到了如下回复：“根据警方记录，Eckelmann 于5月23日离开香港。据信前往南宁，但警方认为他去了别处。实际下落不明。”
为其办理个人保险的香港 Bilman & Co., Ltd. 公司回复：“我们听到的最后消息是，Eckelmann 于5月22日左右离开香港前往海防。”

letter addressed to Eckelmann from J. ... Sons and Friedstedt,

that he had taken no further action in the matter (sic) since all

communicated with Dr. Le Sueur, who replied that he did not know
Eckelmann, had had no word from him and in fact knew little about
the case, since the file had not reached him (from Hanoi).
The lawyers in Hanoi, in their airmailed reply to our enquiry,
expressed great surprise that we had not heard from Eckelmann,
because he had left Hanoi about April 20 (1938), stating that he
was leaving for America by plane, and would probably be in France
in May or June. They gave no details regarding the 'the affaire
that concerned him' but assured us that Eckelmann had not been in
Tonkin since April 20.

...success

Before we associated ourselves with Gerold Eckelmann in the
distribution of his commercial codes, we tried, of course, to get
reports on him. He could give us virtually no references in this
country nor anywhere else but dated back far enough to be of real
value.

Mr. Mullohey, manager of the Commercial Pacific Cable Co. at
Shanghai, replied by cable: "While here found him trustworthy and
hardworking. Always paid bills promptly."

Bank reports added little except to state that Eckelmann was
connected with the Cosmos Trading Co., which had been formed about
1936 by Gerold Eckelmann and F. Unger as a partnership, with a
capital of 80,000 Standard Chinese Dollars; that the company had
opened an account with a local bank in Shanghai, and that it was
reported to be a satisfactory one. "Both of the above mentioned
gentlemen are German and have evidently spent a great deal of their
time in the Far East". (Mr Eckelmann claimed that his company
was The Cosmos Trading Code often confused with the Cosmos Trading
Co., with which he had no connection).

An inquiry sent to J. M. Swan & Co., Shanghai, in June 1937 by
a friend of ours brought the following cable reply: "Gerold Eckelmann
German Formerly Journalist Married Japanese Expelled From Japan
Arrived China Nine Months Ago Now Compiling Cable Code of Little
Merit Has Little Or No Financial Means".

Another report obtained by a friend of ours - we do not know from
what source - stated that no banking references could be obtained;
that the German Consulate of Shanghai said that he was of German
nationality; that he was Editor and Publisher of the Cosmos Trade
Code (sic); that it was said that he had sold about 10,000 books
of his three letter code; that his personal means were moderate;
and that he was honest and capable. It added further that he had

pages.en:
Conclusions:
It is apparent that subject has been obtaining some $50,000.00
from various sources under false pretenses;
that in perpetrating this fraud he uses events that actually
happen and could be readily verified, such as, changing religion,
collision of the S.S. Canton, French transit troubles, etc.
He gave out a number to annoy and embarrass producers, at
which time he was arrested for taking photographs
in prohibited areas - together with his association with a
certain "journalist" from Nanking, which is opposite to HANKOW -
and his sudden disappearance from Nanking and his movements
very suspicious in view of the present Japanese invasion of
HANKOW. There is no evidence that Zuckerman ever went to
CHUNGKING in spite of his oft repeated statements that that
city is his objective.
His affair at Tung King, Tonkin on March 19, 1939 indicates
his passport had been confiscated by the Chinese
authorities in Haiphong and that he wished to avoid an
examination by the French at the Tonkin border.
It is extremely doubtful that Zuckerman ever had any connections
with his so-called Chiang Kai-shek or with Madame Chiang. His
story about his relations with the Generalissimo regarding the
provision of arms of all kinds would sound ridiculous to
anyone who knows him and his claims of having performed special
missions for Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek as a confidential agent
are sheer lies.
Other such statements and claims made by subject are being
investigated. Subject has on various occasions claimed to be
an American Citizen and carried personal cards, according to
French authorities in Tonkin, inscribed in Chinese characters
stating he was an American Citizen.
In the Spring of this year (1939), probably after he disappeared
from the American Hospital in Hong Kong May 23, 1939,
subject approached an American in Shanghai, one H. S. ROTH,
employed by the Shanghai Power Company and made said ROTH
a proposition to rent his American passport for a period of
3 months.

WARNING
Zuckerman is believed to be either mentally deranged or a
dangerous criminal. It is the opinion of the various French
authorities both in Indo-China and Shanghai that subject is
a Japanese spy.
He usually goes armed and apparently is very shrewd. Should
he appear in Chungking he and his belongings, including motor
car, should be thoroughly searched and his movements closely
watched.
Under no circumstances should subject be permitted to contact
the PRESIDENT or MADAME CHIANG KAI-SHEK or any other high
official without due precaution being taken.
pages.zh:
结论：
显然，当事人通过虚假借口从各种来源获取了约50,000.00美元；
在实施这一欺诈行为时，他利用了实际发生且易于核实的事件，例如：改变宗教信仰、“广东”号轮船碰撞、法国过境困难等。
他散布一些号码以骚扰和使生产商难堪，当时他因在禁止区域拍照而被捕——加上他与一名来自南京（与汉口相对）的所谓“记者”的关联，以及他突然从南京消失，鉴于目前日军入侵汉口，其行踪非常可疑。没有证据表明 Zuckerman 曾去过重庆，尽管他反复声称该城市是他的目的地。
他于1939年3月19日在法属印度支那东京（Tung King, Tonkin）的事件表明，他的护照已被海防的中国当局没收，且他希望避免在东京边境接受法国人的检查。
Zuckerman 是否真的与他所谓的蒋介石或蒋夫人有任何联系，极其值得怀疑。他关于就提供各种武器事宜与委员长关系的说法，在任何了解他的人听起来都荒谬可笑，而他声称作为机密特工为蒋介石委员长执行特殊任务的说法纯属谎言。
当事人作出的其他此类陈述和主张正在调查中。当事人曾多次声称自己是美国公民，并持有个人卡片，据法属印度支那东京的法国当局称，卡片上用汉字写明他是美国公民。
今年（1939年）春季，可能在他于1939年5月23日从香港美国医院消失后，当事人在上海接触了一名美国人 H. S. ROTH，此人受雇于上海电力公司，当事人向 ROTH 提出租用其美国护照3个月的提议。

警告
Zuckerman 被认为要么精神错乱，要么是危险的罪犯。法属印度支那和上海的法方各当局均认为当事人是日本间谍。
他通常携带武器，且显然非常狡猾。如果他出现在重庆，应彻底搜查他及其随身物品，包括汽车，并严密监视其行踪。
在任何情况下，除非采取适当的预防措施，否则不得允许当事人接触总统或蒋中正夫人或任何其他高级官员。

Gerald Kurt Eckelman, (German), arrived in
Shanghai from Kobe in 1935, and resided here until
1937. In 1936 he opened an office at 133 Yuen Ming
Yuen Road for the purpose of publishing the "Cosmos
Trading Code", a commercial code which proved a fin-
ancial failure, only a few copies being sold by leading
booksellers in the city. According to reports, this
venture was merely a blind to cover espionage activities.

Eckelman was married to a Japanese and left for
Japan in August 1937. During his sojourn in Shanghai,
he avoided all contact with the local German community
and did not come to the official notice of the Police.
He again arrived in Shanghai in April 30, 1939, in the
S/S. "Rajputana", and left on May 10, 1939 in the S/S.
"Conte Rosso" for Hongkong. While absent from Shanghai
he was in Macao for some time, where he attempted to
buy a passport from a Portugese subject, but the trans-
action was reported to the Portugese authorities.

Eckelman was born in June, 1899, at Neu Oelnitz,
Germany. The passport now in his possession was obtained
at the Reich Consulate in New York on December 16, 1938.

at Haiphong on January 24, 1939, and on January 26
proceeded by plane to Yunnanfu. Shortly afterwards he

杰拉尔德·库尔特·埃克尔曼，（德国人），于1935年从神户抵达上海，并在此居住至1937年。1936年，他在圆明园路133号开设办事处，旨在出版《宇宙贸易密码》（Cosmos Trading Code），这是一种商业密码，但在财务上失败了，市内主要书商仅售出几本。据报告，此举仅仅是掩盖间谍活动的幌子。

埃克尔曼娶了一名日本女子，并于1937年8月前往日本。在上海逗留期间，他避免与当地德国社区有任何接触，也未引起警方的正式注意。他于1939年4月30日再次乘坐“拉杰普塔纳”号轮船（S/S. "Rajputana"）抵达上海，并于1939年5月10日乘坐“孔特·罗索”号轮船（S/S. "Conte Rosso"）离开前往香港。在离开上海期间，他在澳门停留了一段时间，试图从一名葡萄牙籍人士那里购买护照，但该交易已向葡萄牙当局报告。

埃克尔曼于1899年6月出生在德国诺伊厄尔尼茨（Neu Oelnitz）。他目前持有的护照是于1938年12月16日在纽约的德国领事馆获得的。随后他立即离开纽约，于1939年1月24日抵达海防，并于1月26日乘飞机前往云南府。不久之后，他在法属印度支那边境的一个地方与法国当局发生纠纷，该地名未标注中文汉字，记为“Dong-Dang”，但

Subject KARL LUND - recent movements.
Made by D.P.S. Killincock, Forwarded by
With reference to the recent activities of Karl
LUND, alias KNUTSEN, this man arrived in Shanghai on
October 23, 1939, on board the s.s. "Tegelberg".
His heavy baggage had been shipped direct
from Rangoon, and consigned to Shanghai, c/o Messrs
Thos. Cook & Sons.
Lund called at Messrs Cooks and accepted
delivery of his luggage, giving his address as c/o
American Exporters, Room 513, 51 Canton Road. A motor-
car was also included in the consignment lists, but
up to the present, it has not arrived in Shanghai.
The American Exporters occupy Rooms 513 and
514, at 51 Canton Road, and an inscription on the
door reads "American Exporters. Agents for Lund Lines."
Since his return to Shanghai, Lund has not had
any further dealings with Messrs American Motors,
Ltd. Inc., but is reported to have been spending
considerable time recently in Messrs Triangle Motors,
99 Route Cardinal Mercier.
Enquiries have not been made at the latter
address, as this procedure would no doubt result in
Lund's being made cognisant of the fact that the Police
were interested in his movements.
Information obtained reveals that Lund is
connected in some way with the well-known Swedish
explorer and traveller, Sven HEDIN.
D.C. (Special Branch).
J. Killincock

Sir,

Reference the correspondence resting with your
Letter No. D9408 dated the 7th October 1939, I have
the honour to state that Karl Lund arrived here from
the Straits Settlements by steamer on 4th October 1939
but was not permitted to land pending enquiries.
He did not await the result of my enquiries however
but left by air for Penang on 9th October 1939, having
booked thence by train to Singapore. He booked his
heavy luggage through Thos. Cook & Sons to Shanghai.
I have sent the Straits Police a copy of your
letter cited above and its enclosure. I have
suggested that this individual be watched, as his
hasty departure from Rangoon before the completion
of enquiries was suspicious.
Lund has no wife or family in Rangoon nor has

I have the honour to be,

With reference to the cable from the Commissioner
of Police Rangoon, enquiries made at the Swedish Consulate
General show that this person did not register there
and is unknown to the officials. According to the
passport office of U.S.A. Consulate no visas were
issued on November 19, 1938, and it will entail
considerable time to ascertain whether or not a visa
was issued to Lund. Lund visited Shanghai in 1933 and
again in 1939, leaving on the S.S. JAX on September 3,
1939. In August, 1939, he had business dealings with
American Motors Ltd. Inc., 444 Avenue Foch, concerning
the purchase of 12 trucks but the deal failed to
materialize owing to the fact that American Motors were
unable to guarantee safe delivery in Rangoon. Meanwhile
he purchased two passenger buses from Nanking Importers
& Exporters, 12 The Bund and one from Albert Motors,
67 Avenue Roi Albert. In his dealings with American
Motors, he represented himself as Captain Knutsen,
stating that his wife and family were residing in
Rangoon where he conducted a motor agency. He stated
that he had seen service in the Chinese Air Force in
support of which claim, he produced several photographs.
He carried about large sums of money in American
currency and paid cash in all transactions. Nothing
is known to his detriment. Incidentally American Motors
received a telephone call from a friend of Lund or
Knutsen on October 6 stating that he had received a
